current_law_statement: Sessions reviewed: 2024 Regular Session (Act 2024-278 / SB270, eff. Oct. 1, 2024 — rewrote Ala. Code §§ 36-12-40, -41 and added §§ 36-12-43 to -46), 2025 Regular Session, 2026 Regular Session (Act 2026-592 / SB272 added § 36-12-47, redaction of financial identifiers in public-contract records, eff. Apr. 16, 2026 — no fee content). Codified text opened on the Legislature's official Code of Alabama viewer (alison.legislature.state.al.us, GraphQL section content current through Act 2026-592); the enrolled Act 2024-278 PDF was also opened. Section histories for §§ 36-12-40 to -46 show only Act 2024-278, so no 2025–2026 amendment touched the fee/payment provisions. Alabama has no administrative code governing municipal public-records fees (§ 36-12-45(a)(4)); the only figures in state law are Governor's Executive Order No. 734 (Jan. 26, 2023) caps that bind state executive-branch agencies only. Guidance-vs-law gaps: (1) the codified § 36-12-44(a)(3) reads '10 business days' while the enrolled act reads '10 days' (non-fee; flag for the deadlines pass); (2) Attorney General opinions cited by secondary sources for the proposition that reasonable fees may include retrieval/staff time but not attorney review time (AGO 1995-266, 1995-268, 2008-030, 2008-073, 2013-040) could not be opened on the AG's Tyler content-manager viewer and are NOT relied on; (3) municipalities set fees under 'a reasonable fee set by the public officer' with no statewide rate, ceiling, waiver, deposit-threshold or estimate-window figure. Official links: the Legislature's Code of Alabama viewer has no stable per-section URL; rows carry the viewer root as official_link, the enrolled Act 2024-278 PDF as alt_official_link, and section text was pulled from the viewer's GraphQL endpoint (https://alison.legislature.state.al.us/graphql, query codeOfAlabamaSection, displayId '36-12-44').

resolutions.source_language: The public officer may require the requester to pay a reasonable fee set by the public officer before the requester may receive any public records. If the public officer elects to charge a fee, the public officer shall notify the requester of the estimated fee and withhold any public records until receipt of payment. The requester may opt not to pay the fee and thus not receive any substantive response. Additionally, the public officer shall have the discretion to require the requester to pay all or a portion of the estimated fee prior to searching for any responsive public records. | § 36-12-41: Every public officer having custody of a public record that a resident has a right to inspect shall provide him or her, on proper request as provided in this article, with a copy of the public record, on payment of a reasonable fee, as further provided in this article.
resolutions.effective_status: Current; Act 2024-278 effective October 1, 2024; no amendment to the fee provisions in the 2025 or 2026 Regular Sessions (codified history through Act 2026-592 shows only Act 2024-278)
resolutions.notes: No statewide per-page rate or ceiling for municipalities; the operative standard is 'a reasonable fee set by the public officer' (standard request: may charge; time-intensive request: shall charge). Article applies to every 'public officer' (state, county, municipal) except the judicial branch/Art. VI offices (§ 36-12-40(b)). Agency regime (does NOT bind municipalities): Governor's Executive Order No. 734 §4 caps state executive-branch agency fees (up to $20.00/hour incl. $20 minimum for retrieval/preparation; no charge for legal review/redaction; up to $0.50/page for 8.5x11 paper copies; no per-page fee for electronic delivery; actual costs with advance notice) — recorded as AL-9006..AL-9008. Official link is the Legislature's Code of Alabama viewer (browse Title 36 > Chapter 12 > Article 3; section text also served by its GraphQL endpoint https://alison.legislature.state.al.us/graphql, query codeOfAlabamaSection); alternate direct text: enrolled Act 2024-278 PDF.

resolutions.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-44(a)(2), (b)(2); § 36-12-43(b)(4),(6) (redaction time counts toward the 8-hour classification); § 36-21-213(b)
resolutions.source_language: (4) STANDARD REQUEST. A public records request that seeks one or more specifically and discretely identified public records that the public officer determines would take less than eight hours of staff time to process considering the time needed to identify and retrieve any responsive records and any time needed to redact or take other measures to withhold protected information. [...] (6) TIME-INTENSIVE REQUEST. A public records request that the public officer determines would take more than eight hours of staff time to process considering the time needed to identify and retrieve any responsive records and any time needed to redact or take other measures to withhold protected information. | § 36-21-213(b): A custodial law enforcement agency may charge a reasonable fee for redaction and editing of a recording.
resolutions.effective_status: Current; Act 2024-278 effective October 1, 2024; no amendment to the fee provisions in the 2025 or 2026 Regular Sessions (codified history through Act 2026-592 shows only Act 2024-278)
resolutions.manual_verification: Article 3 neither authorizes nor forbids charging for redaction/review; redaction time is expressly part of the staff time that classifies a request. AGO 2008-073 (secondary summaries: attorney review time not chargeable) could not be opened — human legal review before configuring a review/redaction rate.
resolutions.notes: For municipalities no figure; general reasonable-fee standard. Redaction/editing of law-enforcement recordings expressly chargeable at a 'reasonable fee' (§ 36-21-213(b)). Contrast: EO 734 §4.a forbids STATE agencies from charging for legal review or redaction (state_agencies_only). new_rules.atomic_rule: A state executive-branch agency may charge a per-page fee of up to $0.50 for copies on standard 8.5x11 paper and may not charge a per-page fee for documents provided electronically.
new_rules.trigger: Public-records request to a state executive-branch agency
new_rules.source_language: Per-page fees. The agency may charge a per-page fee of up to $.50 for copies produced on standard 8.5x11 paper. The agency may not charge a per-page fee for documents provided electronically.
new_rules.effective_status: Current per the State's public-records portal as of 2026-08-19; requires manual verification whether amended after Act 2024-278
new_rules.notes: STATE EXECUTIVE-BRANCH AGENCIES ONLY; does not bind municipalities.

new_rules.legal_concept: State executive-branch agency actual-cost pass-through with advance notice (EO 734)
new_rules.atomic_rule: A state executive-branch agency may charge actual costs incurred in processing a request (e.g., flash drive/hardware, special paper sizes, electronic-database search costs) if the requester is informed of the cost in advance.
new_rules.trigger: Actual cost item incurred; requester informed in advance
new_rules.source_language: Actual costs. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the agency may charge any actual costs incurred while processing or responding to a public-records request—for example, for a flash drive or other hardware necessary for electronically producing records, for special paper sizes, and for costs associated with searching electronic databases—if the requester is informed of the cost in advance of being charged.
new_rules.effective_status: Current per the State's public-records portal as of 2026-08-19; requires manual verification whether amended after Act 2024-278
new_rules.notes: STATE EXECUTIVE-BRANCH AGENCIES ONLY; does not bind municipalities.

new_rules.legal_concept: Officer may process a request less expensively (no bar to charging less)
new_rules.atomic_rule: Nothing in Article 3 prohibits a public officer from processing a public records request in a manner that is less expensive or more prompt from the requester's perspective.
new_rules.source_language: Nothing in this article shall be construed to prohibit a public officer from processing a public records request in a manner that is less expensive or more prompt from the perspective of the requester.
new_rules.effective_status: Current; Act 2024-278 effective October 1, 2024; no amendment to the fee provisions in the 2025 or 2026 Regular Sessions (codified history through Act 2026-592 shows only Act 2024-278)
new_rules.notes: Supports discretionary fee reduction/waiver and free-allowance policies; does not state grounds. applicability_notes: Ala. Code Title 36 ch. 12 art. 3 binds every 'public officer' (state, county, municipal) except the judicial branch and Art. VI constitutional offices (§ 36-12-40(b)); all statute-based resolutions are applies_to=all_public_bodies and resolve for municipalities directly.

Executive Order No. 734 fee caps ($20/hr, $20 minimum, $0.50/page, no redaction charge) apply to 'any agency, department, board, office, commission, or other entity within the executive branch of state government' (§7) — recorded as guidance for the agency regime only (AL-9006..AL-9008); municipalities are NOT bound and their items resolve to the reasonable-fee soft standard, not to these numbers.
§ 11-103-1 (card payments) is the local-government analogue of § 41-1-60 (state agencies); the municipal item cites § 11-103-1 only.
§ 36-21-213(b) (recording redaction fee) binds any custodial law enforcement agency including municipal police departments; it is record-specific and does not set a general municipal A/V rate.
§ 11-98-12(d)(1) (911 transcript fee not to exceed actual cost of transcription) binds emergency communications districts, not the city clerk; noted, not used to resolve a municipal item.
material_negatives: No statewide per-page copy rate, ceiling or floor for municipalities; the only standard is 'a reasonable fee set by the public officer' (§ 36-12-44(a)(2), (b)(2); § 36-12-41).
No labor rate, labor threshold, overhead multiplier, time increment, free-hours or per-requestor free-time allowance in state law.

No estimate response window, revised-estimate trigger or estimate validity period; no deposit dollar threshold or percentage (other than the implicit 100%-of-estimate bound); no de-minimis, minimum fee, commercial-purpose schedule, fee-waiver grounds, forfeiture, or repeat/aggregation rule.
No general certification-fee provision for municipal records after Act 2024-278 removed 'certified copy' from § 36-12-41.
No administrative rule or AG-adopted fee schedule exists for local bodies (§ 36-12-45(a)(4)); the state's own portal fee schedule (EO 734) is agency-only.
The Code of Alabama full-text search found no municipal-general per-page copy fee statute (hits were probate, license-commissioner, voter-list and Secretary of State schedules — custodian-specific).
